The record is written to `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/reader/h3-ghsa-gcv8-gh4r-25x6.json`. My verdict is that the candidate is usable, but the stacking is thin: all five traps sit in one function, `URI.parse` (`src/URI.js:490-546`).

**Pinned state:** The pinned commit comes before both the A fix and the B fix. `CHANGELOG.md:5` stops at 1.19.6, and `parse` has no scheme-normalisation step. I didn't read git history, so this ordering is an inference.

**Protection:** There is one: `parse` should find the same host a browser would. Right now it only does that when exactly `//` follows the scheme (`src/URI.js:529`) or the input starts with exactly `//` (`src/URI.js:516`). A and B are closed by the same guard, so they count as one.

**Traps, in 4 independent groups:**

| Group | Trap | Mechanism | Type | Tier (DeepSeek / MiMo) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **T1** (advisory A): any other number or mix of slashes and backslashes after a web scheme becomes a URN path with no host (`:529-536`) | M8 | neither | easy / easy |
| 1 | **T2** (advisory B): the same thing with an upper-case scheme. It's a case variant of T1 and only shows up once T1 is fixed with a lowercase-only list | M8 | neither | easy / easy |
| 2 | **T3**: input with no scheme, like `\\host`, `/\host` or `///host`, goes down a separate branch into `parseAuthority` (`:516-521`). Reason to dismiss: "no scheme, so it's just a path" | M1 | deepseek | hard / medium |
| 3 | **T4**: inputs that must keep parsing as they do now (the fix can't over-harden them): `food:///test/file.csv` (`test/urls.js:634`), `file:///…` (`:1310`), the `user:pass@…` URN (`:489`), `://user…` (`:537`), `mailto:` and `javascript:` | M11 | mimo | medium / hard |
| 4 | **T5**: leading whitespace and tab/newline characters are never stripped before the scheme is read (`:490-526`). Reason to dismiss: "trimming input is the caller's job" | M8 | deepseek | hard / medium |

**Conflicts:** The obvious fix for T1, which is to collapse slash runs or accept `scheme:` with no slashes for every scheme, breaks the T4 tests. Stripping all whitespace for T5 would also change URLs that legitimately contain spaces.

**Design:** I recommend using all of T1–T5, with T3 and T4 doing the real work. Without them, T1 and T2 come down to one easy regex. The weakness is that a single well-informed normalisation pass at the top of `parse` closes T1, T2, T3 and T5 together. Estimated effort is about 35 minutes.

**Fairness:** Hidden tests must not expect `file:` to be normalised, because existing tests expect `file:///` to have no host.

**Unconfirmed and out of scope:**
- The claims that A's code left B open and that B lives in code A wrote come from my memory of upstream. A's code isn't in the pinned checkout.
- T3 and T5 look like they were fixed by later urijs advisories, outside this candidate's two. I didn't check those advisory IDs.
- One case-sensitive scheme check (`src/URI.js:1084`) is not recorded as a trap. It only applies when an opt-in flag is set, and it's a spelling variant, so the rules exclude it.
